title: Simplifying Expressions with Integers: GEMDAS and Number Properties
seo_title: Grade 7 GEMDAS Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 7)
standard_text: Simplify numerical expressions involving integers using number properties and the order of operations (GEMDAS).
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 GEMDAS worksheets for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: order of operations with integers, grouping symbols, exponents, number properties and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: × and ÷ (and + and −) go left to right.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • GEMDAS: Grouping symbols first, then Exponents, then Multiplication and Division (left to right), then Addition and Subtraction (left to right).
  • Grouping symbols include parentheses ( ), brackets [ ] and fraction bars.
  • (−3)² = 9, but −3² = −9: the exponent acts only on what it touches.
  • Number properties (commutative, associative, distributive) can make the work easier: 4 × 17 × 25 = (4 × 25) × 17.

Examples

Example

−2 + 3 × (4 − 7)²

(−3)² = 9

3 × 9 = 27

−2 + 27

Answer: 25

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding first× and ÷ come before + and −.
× before an earlier ÷Work left to right.
−3² as 9Only (−3)² is 9.

faq.q: What does MATATAG Math 7 ask about GEMDAS?
faq.a: Simplify numerical expressions involving integers using number properties and the order of operations (GEMDAS).

faq.q: What does the G in GEMDAS stand for?
faq.a: Grouping symbols, such as parentheses and brackets.

faq.q: Is GEMDAS the same as PEMDAS?
faq.a: Yes. P (parentheses) is one kind of grouping symbol.

faq.q: Do I always multiply before dividing?
faq.a: No. Do them in order from left to right.

items.q: Which part of 40 − 30 ÷ 5 do you work out first?
items.e: 40 − 30 ÷ 5 = 40 − 6 = 34. Divide before you subtract.

items.q: Two soccer teams, with 18 and 14 players, share 96 orange slices equally. How many slices does each player get?
items.e: One expression: 96 ÷ (18 + 14). 96 ÷ (18 + 14) = 96 ÷ 32 = 3, so 3 slices. Not 64 slices: that subtracts instead of dividing. Not 32 slices: that is the number of players, not slices. Not 48 slices: that shares between the 2 teams, not between the players.

items.q: In a class quiz game, a correct answer scores 5 points and a wrong answer scores −3 points. Mark gets 7 correct and 9 wrong. What is her score?
items.e: One expression: 7 × 5 + 9 × (−3). 7 × 5 + 9 × (−3) = 35 + 9 × (−3) = 35 + (−27) = 8, so 8 points. Not −132 points: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not 62 points: that comes from a sign error: a negative and a positive multiplied or divided give a negative. Not 35 points: that stops one step too early.

items.q: A box lacrosse team of 12 players has 4 cases of 24 water bottles. They give 12 bottles to the coaches and share the rest equally among the players. How many bottles does each player get?
items.e: One expression: (4 × 24 − 12) ÷ 12. (4 × 24 − 12) ÷ 12 = (96 − 12) ÷ 12 = 84 ÷ 12 = 7, so 7 bottles. Not 95 bottles: that comes from ignoring the brackets. Not 84 bottles: that forgets to share among the players. Not 9 bottles: that adds the coaches’ bottles instead of taking them away.
